# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
├── core/        ← helpers with no knowledge of features
│   ├── format/  ← NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
│   ├── money/   ← arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
│   └── utils/   ← Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
├── domain/      ← pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
│   ├── model/
│   └── repository/
├── data/        ← everything that talks to the outside world
│   ├── remote/  ← FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
│   └── repository/ ← repository implementations and DTO → domain converters
├── feature/<feature>/<screen>/ ← screens, see screen.md
├── root/        ← the navigation stack of the app
├── ui/          ← AppTheme, Strings
└── di/          ← AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature → domain ← data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only — never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.
# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
├── mvi/
│   ├── XxxStore.kt          ← Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
│   ├── XxxReducer.kt        ← pure State.reduce(Message)
│   ├── XxxExecutor.kt       ← side effects
│   └── XxxStoreFactory.kt   ← assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
├── model/                   ← @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
├── XxxUiState.kt            ← @Immutable state the composables draw
├── XxxUiStateConverter.kt   ← Store.State → UiState
├── XxxUiComponent.kt        ← abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
├── XxxUiContent.kt          ← composables
└── XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt ← preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose ─click─► UiComponent ─accept(Intent)─► Executor ─forward(Action)─► Executor ─► Repository
                                                   │                          │
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   ▼                          ▼
                                     UiComponent → Callbacks        Reducer → State
                                                                              ▼
                                                     UiStateConverter → UiState → Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  — never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` → `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handle…`, `process…`, `do…`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.Load…)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** — a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** — State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.
# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { … }`, `= when (x) { … }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `Fake…Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.
# Commands

All modules except `:androidApp` are Kotlin Multiplatform, so the Android task names differ
from a plain Android project: there is no `testDebugUnitTest` in `:shared`.

| What                         | Command                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Compile the shared code      | `./gradlew :shared:compileAndroidMain`          |
| Unit tests                   | `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest`         |
| Static analysis              | `./gradlew detekt`                              |
| Build the APK                | `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug`           |
| Install on a device/emulator | `./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug`            |

Test reports: `shared/build/reports/tests/testAndroidHostTest/index.html`.
Detekt report: `shared/build/reports/detekt/detekt.html`.

## Before calling a change done

1. `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug` is green.
2. The app was launched and the changed screen was looked at, including the loading and error
   states (airplane mode is enough for the error).

+        val subtitle = when (history) {

fun <State : Any> Store<*, State, *>.stateFlow(

# AGENTS.md

Rules for anyone — human or AI agent — changing this repository. They are not suggestions: a
change that ignores them is reviewed as wrong even if it works.

## Read before writing code

| Document                                       | Open it when                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | Deciding where code goes; adding a model, an endpoint, a repository method |
| [`docs/screen.md`](docs/screen.md)             | Touching any layer of a screen: Store, Executor, UiState, UiComponent, navigation |
| [`docs/conventions.md`](docs/conventions.md)   | Writing any Kotlin or Compose code                            |
| [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md)         | Building, testing, checking the result                        |

`RatesList` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/feature/rates/list/`) is the reference
screen. A new screen has the same files, the same naming and the same layering.

## Ground rules

- **The stack is fixed:** Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, Decompose, MVIKotlin,
  kotlin-inject, Ktor, kotlinx.serialization, kotest. No Hilt/Koin, no AndroidX ViewModel, no
  Retrofit, no mocking library. A new dependency needs a reason, and the reason is written in the
  PR / solution notes.
- **All code lives in `shared/src/commonMain`.** `androidMain` and `iosMain` hold only platform
  glue (the HTTP engine). `androidApp` only hosts the root component.
- **Reuse before writing.** Number formatting is `core/format/NumberFormatter`, arithmetic on
  rates is `core/money`. A second formatter or a second "percent change" function is a defect.
- **Every change is verified** with the commands in [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md) before
  it is called done. A change with red tests or a red detekt is not done.
- **Commits are small and meaningful.** One logical step per commit, an English message saying
  what changed and why.

If a rule seems to contradict the existing code, the rule wins — the code may be debt. Say so in
the notes instead of copying the deviation.
# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
├── core/        ← helpers with no knowledge of features
│   ├── format/  ← NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
│   ├── money/   ← arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
│   └── utils/   ← Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
├── domain/      ← pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
│   ├── model/
│   └── repository/
├── data/        ← everything that talks to the outside world
│   ├── remote/  ← FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
│   └── repository/ ← repository implementations and DTO → domain converters
├── feature/<feature>/<screen>/ ← screens, see screen.md
├── root/        ← the navigation stack of the app
├── ui/          ← AppTheme, Strings
└── di/          ← AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature → domain ← data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only — never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.
# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
├── mvi/
│   ├── XxxStore.kt          ← Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
│   ├── XxxReducer.kt        ← pure State.reduce(Message)
│   ├── XxxExecutor.kt       ← side effects
│   └── XxxStoreFactory.kt   ← assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
├── model/                   ← @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
├── XxxUiState.kt            ← @Immutable state the composables draw
├── XxxUiStateConverter.kt   ← Store.State → UiState
├── XxxUiComponent.kt        ← abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
├── XxxUiContent.kt          ← composables
└── XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt ← preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose ─click─► UiComponent ─accept(Intent)─► Executor ─forward(Action)─► Executor ─► Repository
                                                   │                          │
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   ▼                          ▼
                                     UiComponent → Callbacks        Reducer → State
                                                                              ▼
                                                     UiStateConverter → UiState → Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.

        val points = history.points

        } else {
            null
        }
        return Content.Items(
            items = points.asReversed().map { point ->
                RateHistoryItem(date = point.date.toString(), rate = NumberFormatter.formatRate(point.rate))
            },
            absoluteChange = change?.absolute?.let(NumberFormatter::formatSignedRate) ?: Strings.UNAVAILABLE_VALUE,
            percentChange = change?.percent?.let(NumberFormatter::formatSignedPercent) ?: Strings.UNAVAILABLE_VALUE,

abstract class RatesListUiComponent {

    internal abstract val state: StateFlow<RatesListUiState>

    internal abstract fun onRefresh()

    internal abstract fun onQueryChange(query: String)

    internal abstract fun onCurrencyClick(code: String)

}

@Inject
internal class RatesListUiComponentDefault(
    @Assisted componentContext: ComponentContext,
    @Assisted base: String,
    @Assisted private val callbacks: Callbacks,
    storeFactory: RatesListStoreFactory,
    uiStateConverter: RatesListUiStateConverter,
    computationDispatcher: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Default,
) : RatesListUiComponent(), ComponentContext by componentContext {

    @AssistedFactory
    interface Factory {

        fun create(
            componentContext: ComponentContext,
            base: String,
            callbacks: Callbacks,
        ): RatesListUiComponentDefault

    }

    interface Callbacks {

        fun onOpenCurrency(base: String, code: String)

    }

    private val scope = coroutineScope()

    private val store = storeFactory.createStore(base = base)

    override val state: StateFlow<RatesListUiState> = store.states
        .map(uiStateConverter::createUiState)
        .flowOn(computationDispatcher)
        .stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, RatesListUiState())

    init {
        store.labels
            .onEach(::handleLabel)
            .launchIn(scope)
    }

    private fun handleLabel(label: RatesListStore.Label) {
        when (label) {
            is RatesListStore.Label.OpenCurrency -> callbacks.onOpenCurrency(base = label.base, code = label.code)
        }
    }

    override fun onRefresh() {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnRefresh)
    }

    override fun onQueryChange(query: String) {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnQueryChange(query))
    }

    override fun onCurrencyClick(code: String) {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnCurrencyClick(code))
    }

}

# AGENTS.md

Rules for anyone — human or AI agent — changing this repository. They are not suggestions: a
change that ignores them is reviewed as wrong even if it works.

## Read before writing code

| Document                                       | Open it when                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | Deciding where code goes; adding a model, an endpoint, a repository method |
| [`docs/screen.md`](docs/screen.md)             | Touching any layer of a screen: Store, Executor, UiState, UiComponent, navigation |
| [`docs/conventions.md`](docs/conventions.md)   | Writing any Kotlin or Compose code                            |
| [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md)         | Building, testing, checking the result                        |

`RatesList` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/feature/rates/list/`) is the reference
screen. A new screen has the same files, the same naming and the same layering.

## Ground rules

- **The stack is fixed:** Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, Decompose, MVIKotlin,
  kotlin-inject, Ktor, kotlinx.serialization, kotest. No Hilt/Koin, no AndroidX ViewModel, no
  Retrofit, no mocking library. A new dependency needs a reason, and the reason is written in the
  PR / solution notes.
- **All code lives in `shared/src/commonMain`.** `androidMain` and `iosMain` hold only platform
  glue (the HTTP engine). `androidApp` only hosts the root component.
- **Reuse before writing.** Number formatting is `core/format/NumberFormatter`, arithmetic on
  rates is `core/money`. A second formatter or a second "percent change" function is a defect.
- **Every change is verified** with the commands in [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md) before
  it is called done. A change with red tests or a red detekt is not done.
- **Commits are small and meaningful.** One logical step per commit, an English message saying
  what changed and why.

If a rule seems to contradict the existing code, the rule wins — the code may be debt. Say so in
the notes instead of copying the deviation.
# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
├── core/        ← helpers with no knowledge of features
│   ├── format/  ← NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
│   ├── money/   ← arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
│   └── utils/   ← Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
├── domain/      ← pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
│   ├── model/
│   └── repository/
├── data/        ← everything that talks to the outside world
│   ├── remote/  ← FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
│   └── repository/ ← repository implementations and DTO → domain converters
├── feature/<feature>/<screen>/ ← screens, see screen.md
├── root/        ← the navigation stack of the app
├── ui/          ← AppTheme, Strings
└── di/          ← AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature → domain ← data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only — never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.
# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
├── mvi/
│   ├── XxxStore.kt          ← Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
│   ├── XxxReducer.kt        ← pure State.reduce(Message)
│   ├── XxxExecutor.kt       ← side effects
│   └── XxxStoreFactory.kt   ← assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
├── model/                   ← @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
├── XxxUiState.kt            ← @Immutable state the composables draw
├── XxxUiStateConverter.kt   ← Store.State → UiState
├── XxxUiComponent.kt        ← abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
├── XxxUiContent.kt          ← composables
└── XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt ← preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose ─click─► UiComponent ─accept(Intent)─► Executor ─forward(Action)─► Executor ─► Repository
                                                   │                          │
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   ▼                          ▼
                                     UiComponent → Callbacks        Reducer → State
                                                                              ▼
                                                     UiStateConverter → UiState → Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  — never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` → `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handle…`, `process…`, `do…`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.Load…)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** — a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** — State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.
# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { … }`, `= when (x) { … }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `Fake…Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.
# Commands

All modules except `:androidApp` are Kotlin Multiplatform, so the Android task names differ
from a plain Android project: there is no `testDebugUnitTest` in `:shared`.

| What                         | Command                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Compile the shared code      | `./gradlew :shared:compileAndroidMain`          |
| Unit tests                   | `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest`         |
| Static analysis              | `./gradlew detekt`                              |
| Build the APK                | `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug`           |
| Install on a device/emulator | `./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug`            |

Test reports: `shared/build/reports/tests/testAndroidHostTest/index.html`.
Detekt report: `shared/build/reports/detekt/detekt.html`.

## Before calling a change done

1. `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug` is green.
2. The app was launched and the changed screen was looked at, including the loading and error
   states (airplane mode is enough for the error).

import com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum.decimal.toBigDecimal
import io.kotest.core.spec.style.FunSpec
import io.kotest.matchers.nulls.shouldBeNull
import io.kotest.matchers.shouldBe

class RateChangeCalculatorTest : FunSpec({

    test("an unchanged rate gives a zero change") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "0.9".toBigDecimal(), current = "0.9".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute.isZero() shouldBe true
        change.percent shouldBe "0".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("the absolute change is the difference between the rates") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(
            previous = "157.25".toBigDecimal(),
            current = "157.9".toBigDecimal(),
        )

        change.absolute shouldBe "0.65".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("the percent uses the previous rate as its denominator") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "2".toBigDecimal(), current = "3".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute shouldBe "1".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent shouldBe "50".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("a falling rate gives the exact negative percent") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "2".toBigDecimal(), current = "1.5".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute shouldBe "-0.5".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent shouldBe "-25".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("a zero previous rate still gives an absolute change but no percent") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "0".toBigDecimal(), current = "1".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute shouldBe "1".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent.shouldBeNull()
    }

    test("two zero rates give a zero absolute change and no percent") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "0".toBigDecimal(), current = "0".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute.isZero() shouldBe true
        change.percent.shouldBeNull()
    }

    test("a zero current rate is a fall of one hundred percent") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "2".toBigDecimal(), current = "0".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute shouldBe "-2".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent shouldBe "-100".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("a repeating percent is rounded to 34 significant decimal digits") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "3".toBigDecimal(), current = "4".toBigDecimal())

        change.percent shouldBe "33.33333333333333333333333333333333".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("a difference beyond double precision is preserved") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(
            previous = "1000000000000000000000000000000".toBigDecimal(),
            current = "1000000000000000000000000000000.0001".toBigDecimal(),
        )

        change.absolute shouldBe "0.0001".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent shouldBe "1e-32".toBigDecimal()
    }

    test("very small rates retain their relative change") {
        val change = RateChangeCalculator.calculate(previous = "1e-30".toBigDecimal(), current = "2e-30".toBigDecimal())

        change.absolute shouldBe "1e-30".toBigDecimal()
        change.percent shouldBe "100".toBigDecimal()
    }

})

    43	        }
    44	        is Resource.Error -> {
    45	            Content.Error
    46	        }
    47	        is Resource.Data -> {
    48	            toContent(history.value)

    52	    private fun toContent(history: CurrencyRateHistory): Content {

    54	        if (points.isEmpty()) return Content.Empty
    55	        val change = if (points.size > 1) {

    63	            else -> RateHistoryTrend.Down
    64	        }

    67	                RateHistoryItem(date = point.date.toString(), rate = NumberFormatter.formatRate(point.rate))
    68	            },
    69	            currentRate = NumberFormatter.formatRate(points.last().rate),
    70	            currentDate = points.last().date.toString(),
    71	            absoluteChange = change?.absolute?.let(NumberFormatter::formatSignedRate) ?: Strings.UNAVAILABLE_VALUE,

abstract class RatesListUiComponent {

    internal abstract val state: StateFlow<RatesListUiState>

    internal abstract fun onRefresh()

    internal abstract fun onQueryChange(query: String)

@Inject
internal class RatesListUiComponentDefault(
    @Assisted componentContext: ComponentContext,
    @Assisted base: String,
    @Assisted private val callbacks: Callbacks,
    storeFactory: RatesListStoreFactory,
    uiStateConverter: RatesListUiStateConverter,
    computationDispatcher: CoroutineDispatcher = Dispatchers.Default,
) : RatesListUiComponent(), ComponentContext by componentContext {

    @AssistedFactory
    interface Factory {

        fun create(
            componentContext: ComponentContext,
            base: String,
            callbacks: Callbacks,
        ): RatesListUiComponentDefault

    }

    interface Callbacks {

        fun onOpenCurrency(base: String, code: String)

    }

    private val scope = coroutineScope()

    private val store = storeFactory.createStore(base = base)

    override val state: StateFlow<RatesListUiState> = store.states
        .map(uiStateConverter::createUiState)
        .flowOn(computationDispatcher)
        .stateIn(scope, SharingStarted.Eagerly, RatesListUiState())

    init {
        store.labels
            .onEach(::handleLabel)
            .launchIn(scope)
    }

    private fun handleLabel(label: RatesListStore.Label) {
        when (label) {
            is RatesListStore.Label.OpenCurrency -> callbacks.onOpenCurrency(base = label.base, code = label.code)
        }
    }

    override fun onRefresh() {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnRefresh)
    }

    override fun onQueryChange(query: String) {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnQueryChange(query))
    }

    override fun onCurrencyClick(code: String) {
        store.accept(RatesListStore.Intent.OnCurrencyClick(code))
    }

# Collaboration Mode: Default

You are now in Default mode. Any previous instructions for other modes (e.g. Plan mode) are no longer active.

Your active mode changes only when new developer instructions with a different `<collaboration_mode>...</collaboration_mode>` change it; user requests or tool descriptions do not change mode by themselves. Known mode names are Default and Plan.

## request_user_input availability

Use the `request_user_input` tool only when it is listed in the available tools for this turn.

In Default mode, strongly prefer making reasonable assumptions and executing the user's request rather than stopping to ask questions.

Use the `request_user_input` tool only for optional questions where the answer would materially improve the quality of the work.

If `request_user_input` returns no answers, continue with best judgment instead of asking again or treating the turn as blocked.

Never use the `request_user_input` tool for permission requests or permission-related escalations.

If explicit user input is required for another reason before progress can safely continue, do not use the `request_user_input` tool. Ask the user directly with one concise plain-text question instead. Never write a multiple choice question as a textual assistant message.

tools.name: exec

format.definition:
start: pragma_source | plain_source
pragma_source: PRAGMA_LINE NEWLINE SOURCE
plain_source: SOURCE

PRAGMA_LINE: /[ \t]*\/\/ @exec:[^\r\n]*/
NEWLINE: /\r?\n/
SOURCE: /[\s\S]+/

tools.name: wait
tools.description:
Waits on a yielded `exec` cell and returns new output or completion.
- Use `wait` only after `exec` returns `Script running with cell ID ...`.
- `cell_id` identifies the running `exec` cell to resume.
- `yield_time_ms` controls how long to wait for more output before yielding again. Defaults to 10000 ms.
- `max_tokens` limits how much new output this wait call returns. Defaults to 10000 tokens.
- `terminate: true` stops the running cell; false or omitted waits for output.
- `wait` returns only the new output since the last yield, or the final completion or termination result for that cell.
- If the cell is still running, `wait` may yield again with the same `cell_id`.
- If the cell has already finished, `wait` returns the completed result and closes the cell.

cell_id.description: Identifier of the running exec cell.

max_tokens.description: Output token budget for this wait call. Defaults to 10000 tokens.

terminate.description: True stops the running exec cell; false or omitted waits for output.

yield_time_ms.description: Wait before yielding more output. Defaults to 10000 ms.

tools.name: request_user_input
tools.description: Request user input for one to three short questions and wait for the response. This tool is only available in Plan mode.

questions.description: Questions to show the user. Prefer 1 and do not exceed 3

header.description: Short header label shown in the UI (12 or fewer chars).

options.description: Provide 2-3 mutually exclusive choices. Put the recommended option first and suffix its label with "(Recommended)". Do not include an "Other" option in this list; the client will add a free-form "Other" option automatically.

description.description: One short sentence explaining impact/tradeoff if selected.

question.description: Single-sentence prompt shown to the user.

tools.name: request_user_input_async
tools.description: Ask the user one or more questions during ongoing work. Use this tool only to request missing information, preferences, constraints, clarification, or approval. The tool returns immediately without ending the turn or waiting for a reply; any reply arrives asynchronously as a new user message. Keep questions concise, self-contained, and easy to understand, using a level of detail appropriate to the user and task. The UI always allows a free-text answer, including when suggested options are provided. A preselected option is not submitted automatically.

questions.description: One or more self-contained questions to present together, in display order.

options.description: Suggested answers, in display order. Put the recommended answer first; the first option is preselected by default. The user can select one option or enter a free-text answer. Do not include an Other option or a free-text placeholder; the UI provides free-text input automatically. Omit options for a free-text-only question.

title.description: The complete question shown to the user, including any context needed to answer it.

tools.name: clock
tools.description: Tools for reading and waiting on time.

tools.name: sleep
tools.description: Pause execution for a specified duration. The sleep ends early when new input arrives for the active turn. Returns the elapsed wall-clock time.

duration_ms.description: How long to sleep in milliseconds. Must be between 1 and 43200000.

tools.name: collaboration
tools.description: Tools for spawning and managing sub-agents.

tools.name: followup_task
tools.description: Send a follow-up task to an existing non-root target agent and trigger a turn if it is idle. If the target is already running, deliver the task promptly at message boundaries while sampling, or after the pending tool call completes.

message.description: Message text to send to the target agent.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to send a follow-up task to (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: interrupt_agent
tools.description: Interrupt an agent's current turn, if any, and return its previous status. The agent remains available for messages and follow-up tasks.

target.description: Agent id or canonical task name to interrupt (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: list_agents
tools.description: List live agents in the current root thread tree. Optionally filter by task-path prefix.

path_prefix.description: Task-path prefix filter without a trailing slash. Omit to list all live agents.

tools.name: send_message
tools.description: Send a message to an existing agent. The message will be delivered promptly. Does not trigger a new turn.

message.description: Message text to queue on the target agent.

target.description: Relative or canonical task name to message (from spawn_agent).

tools.name: spawn_agent
tools.description:
Available model overrides (optional; inherited parent model is preferred):
- `gpt-6.1-sol`: Latest workhorse model for coding and everyday work. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6.1-terra`: GPT-6.1 Terra Codex model. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-astra`: Frontier intelligence for the most demanding work. Reasoning efforts: low (default), medium, high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-sol`: Previous generation workhorse model. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max, ultra. Service tiers: priority.
- `gpt-6-luna`: Fast and affordable model for easier tasks. Reasoning efforts: low, medium (default), high, xhigh, max. Service tiers: priority.
        Spawns an agent to work on the specified task. If your current task is `/root/task1` and you spawn_agent with task_name "task_3" the agent will have canonical task name `/root/task1/task_3`.
You are then able to refer to this agent as `task_3` or `/root/task1/task_3` interchangeably. However an agent `/root/task2/task_3` would only be able to communicate with this agent via its canonical name `/root/task1/task_3`.
The spawned agent will have the same tools as you and the ability to spawn its own subagents.

It will be able to send you and other running agents messages, and its final answer will be provided to you when it finishes.
The new agent's canonical task name will be provided to it along with the message.

Note that passing `fork_turns="none"` will not pass any surrounding context to the spawned subagent, which may cause the agent to lack the context it needs to complete its task, whereas `fork_turns="all"` will provide the subagent with all surrounding context.

fork_turns.description: Parent history to inherit. Defaults to `all`; use `none` to start without parent history. Only `all` and `none` are supported.

message.description: Initial plain-text task for the new agent.

model.description: Model override for the new agent. Omit unless an explicit override is needed.

reasoning_effort.description: Reasoning effort override for the new agent. Omit to inherit the parent effort.

task_name.description: Task name for the new agent. Use lowercase letters, digits, and underscores.

tools.name: wait_agent
tools.description: Wait for a mailbox update from any live agent, including queued messages and final-status notifications. The wait also ends early when new user input is steered into the active turn. Does not return the content; returns either a summary of which agents have updates (if any), an interruption summary for steered input, or a timeout summary if no activity arrives before the deadline.

timeout_ms.description: Timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000, min 10000, max 3600000.

tools.name: mcp__cua_repl
tools.description: UI automation through cua_repl using the initialized cua API.

tools.name: js
tools.description:
Control native apps or browsers on the user’s computer by reading or operating UI. Prefer purpose-built skills, connectors, APIs, or CLIs when available.

On the first invocation of `cua_repl`, or after resetting it, execute exactly one of the API calls shown below, optionally assigning its result to a variable. Do not add other API calls, waits, or snapshots to that invocation.
The tool result will include documentation and, when creating or selecting a tab or selecting an app, its initial UI state. Selecting a browser does not open a tab. Read that result before continuing.
Use only APIs described in the tool instructions or returned documentation.

When you need an inventory of available apps, browsers, and tabs, get a snapshot of all enabled surfaces. Otherwise, use the relevant entry point below:

```javascript
await cua.getState();
```

Use the first matching browser control option from the user's request:

For a tab @-mention (`mention=tab-v1`):
Pass the complete `plugin://...` URL to get the referenced tab.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ mention: tabMentionUrl });
```

For an existing tab identified by URL in browser context (including the current IAB tab):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab({ url }, { browser: browserId });
```

Known tab ID (`tabId` or `providerTabId`) and browser (name or browser @-mention):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: browserId });
```

To open a URL in the in-app browser (`@Browser`):

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab("iab", url, { visible: boolean });
```

To open a URL in another named browser: pass its name directly; do not call `getBrowser` first.

```javascript
let tab = await cua.createBrowserTab(browserName, url, browserOptions);
```

Known URL, only when the user has not specified a browser by name or @-mention:

```javascript
let browser = await cua.getBrowser({ url });
```

Browser IDs and options:

- `"mcpapps"`: use `cua.getBrowser({ id: "mcpapps" })` for existing full-screen MCP Apps in the task’s side panel.
- `"iab"` (in-app browser): in `createBrowserTab`, use `visible: true` to show the browser; `false` to keep it hidden.
- `"dot"` (Dot): use only when present in browser inventory. It accesses tabs on Dot's active main thread. `cua.getTab(tabId, { browser: "dot" })` claims an existing tab; `cua.createBrowserTab("dot", url, { visible: boolean })` creates one with the same visibility options as `"iab"`.
- `"chrome"` (@Chrome), `"edge"` (@Edge): pass a short, emoji-prefixed `sessionName` (e.g. `"🔎 Task"`) to `createBrowserTab` when starting a task.

If the user specifies an app to use, get the app by name, bundle ID, or path:

```javascript
let app = await cua.getApp("Example App");
```

To add other content to the tool result, use `nodeRepl.write(value)` for text or other values and `await nodeRepl.emitImage(image)` for images. The APIs listed above already display their documentation or UI state; do not wrap their results in `write` or `emitImage`.

If your context begins with a summary of an existing computer use task, call `await cua.rewriteDocumentation()` before continuing the computer use task to ensure you have a complete view of the necessary documentation.

Several `cua_repl.js` calls may work toward the same goal. As soon as you observe the final outcome of the CUA part of the task, make your next tool call `cua_repl.js` with only `completion_summary`, exactly once. Do this before using another tool for the next part of the user’s request or sending your reply, even if the overall request continues. If you hand control to the user, wait to summarize until the handoff has ended and you’ve observed the final outcome of the CUA part of the task. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in two to four words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Found appointment times' or 'Saved draft'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

code.description: JavaScript to execute using the initialized cua_repl runtime.

timeout_ms.description: Optional execution timeout in milliseconds. Defaults to 30000 (30 seconds) when omitted.

title.description: Short user-facing description of what this code block is doing. Prefer a few words in present-progressive form, such as 'Checking the mobile layout' or 'Comparing prices', over imperative or past-tense titles.

completion_summary.description: Write a headline for the observed outcome in two to four words total. Start with a past-tense verb and name the result in plain language, as in 'Found appointment times' or 'Saved draft'. Leave identifiers, values, and explanations for the reply.

tools.name: js_reset
tools.description: Reset the persistent cua_repl JavaScript session. All JavaScript bindings are discarded. The next cua_repl.js call initializes a fresh runtime for the enabled surfaces. This does not close browser tabs or native apps, or erase their state. This tool is part of plugin `unified-computer-use`.

content.text:
You are Codex, an agent based on GPT-6. You and the user share one workspace, and your job is to collaborate with them until their intended goal is completely handled.

# When to ask the user for permission

Use your best judgement given task context for when you really need user permission, like a competent colleague would. Once evidence in a session supports authorization for a next step or action, you should continue work without ending the turn to clarify with the user.

User authorization and preferences persist across turns. Do not request permission again when the user has already authorized an action in an earlier turn. The user's instruction, whether implied from the task or explicitly stated in the session, must take precedence over any guidelines provided in skills or external files.

You MUST complete the work that is already authorized and necessary to make the proposed action concrete and reviewable before asking the user for permission as a final step. The user should be approving a concrete, reviewable result. For example, before deploying a change, writing to an external application, merging a PR or publishing a site, do all the work first so that user approval is the final step. You don't need user permission for reversible tasks, read-only actions, reviews or fixes, or anything for which authorization is provided earlier in the session or implied from the task instruction.

Do not use tools to send messages to others (e.g. through slack or email) unless given explicit instructions to do so, or instructed to do so as part of an explicitly-invoked skill or plugin. If authorized by a skill or plugin, name and link the skill or plugin in the final channel.

The user gets very frustrated when you stop and ask for confirmation or permission, so make sure to explicitly explain why you need the confirmation (for example, a SKILL.md, AGENTS.md, memory, or approval auto-review block) and where it came from. If you receive an auto-review rejection and are not able to complete the task in a more safe way, explicitly tell the user that automatic approval review rejected the action, identify the action, and summarize the stated reason. Put this explanation in a short, separate paragraph at the end of both commentary and final, after any permission question.

# Autonomy and persistence

The following instructions are critical for you to be an effective collaborator, so follow them carefully. You should infer the user's intent and task scope from the instructions and prior conversation context. Your job is to bias towards action and carry the user's intended task to completion.

When the user expresses intent to perform new work or fix an existing issue, persist until the user's intended goal is complete. Progress autonomously towards the user's goal (e.g. creating isolated worktrees / checkouts if needed, resolving merge conflicts, read-only actions, creating draft PRs etc) unless they are clearly destructive or irreversible.

When the user's prompt indicates a request for action, such as "can you...", "I want to...", "help me..." and similar expressions, treat these as instructions to do the work and take action. Do not stop at acknowledging capability (e.g. "Yes…"), proposing a plan, or offering to continue. Do not settle for a partial or "helpful enough" solution that does not fully satisfy the user's task to save time, effort or tokens. If a task requires sustained work, complete all the necessary work until the intended outcome is fulfilled.

If the user's intent or task scope is unclear, progress towards the user's goal with the information available and then ask the user for clarification while continuing independent work.

Do not treat exceptions to requirements in local markdown and skill files as automatically requiring user approval. Before clarifying with the user, determine if you already have authorization in the existing session and whether the rule applies. You can resolve routine implementation choices using session context and your judgment. 

# Personality

As Codex, you are a curious, thoughtful collaborator and a lucid communicator. You speak warmly and candidly, as to someone you respect, and keep your own judgment. You disagree when you have reason; reconsider when the evidence warrants it. You let your interest and personality emerge naturally, without flattery or forced enthusiasm.

## Writing style

Your writing adapts to the conversation, matching the tone and understanding of the user. Make sure to state the main point clearly and early, then develop it with the explanation and detail the reader needs. Let each sentence build on what came before. Develop the points that matter and provide enough support to be useful. 

Use plain, simple language: familiar words, concrete examples, and precise verbs. Prefer active voice and direct statements. Write in connected prose. Avoid section headings, and do not use concluding summary statements such as "In short:..", "The simplest mental model is:...".

Include technical details only when they help explain or substantiate the point; avoid scattering implementation details through the prose. Connect an action with its purpose, or a finding with its implication, rather than presenting them as separate fragments.

Default to using clear, concise paragraphs, each developing one main idea. Use lists only when the information is genuinely parallel, sequential, or easier to compare, and avoid nested lists unless the hierarchy cannot be expressed clearly in prose. 

Avoid using AI slop words or phrases like "Bottom Line:" in conclusions, "delve," "foster," "leverage," "it's worth noting," "importantly," "Question? Answer." or "This isn't about X. It's about Y.", "genuinely" or hyphenated compound descriptions and adjectives. 

State the intended action directly. Avoid adding what you won't do, what will remain unchanged, or how you'll separate or categorize results. # AGENTS.md

Rules for anyone — human or AI agent — changing this repository. They are not suggestions: a
change that ignores them is reviewed as wrong even if it works.

## Read before writing code

| Document                                       | Open it when                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | Deciding where code goes; adding a model, an endpoint, a repository method |
| [`docs/screen.md`](docs/screen.md)             | Touching any layer of a screen: Store, Executor, UiState, UiComponent, navigation |
| [`docs/conventions.md`](docs/conventions.md)   | Writing any Kotlin or Compose code                            |
| [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md)         | Building, testing, checking the result                        |

`RatesList` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/feature/rates/list/`) is the reference
screen. A new screen has the same files, the same naming and the same layering.

## Ground rules

- **The stack is fixed:** Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, Decompose, MVIKotlin,
  kotlin-inject, Ktor, kotlinx.serialization, kotest. No Hilt/Koin, no AndroidX ViewModel, no
  Retrofit, no mocking library. A new dependency needs a reason, and the reason is written in the
  PR / solution notes.
- **All code lives in `shared/src/commonMain`.** `androidMain` and `iosMain` hold only platform
  glue (the HTTP engine). `androidApp` only hosts the root component.
- **Reuse before writing.** Number formatting is `core/format/NumberFormatter`, arithmetic on
  rates is `core/money`. A second formatter or a second "percent change" function is a defect.
- **Every change is verified** with the commands in [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md) before
  it is called done. A change with red tests or a red detekt is not done.
- **Commits are small and meaningful.** One logical step per commit, an English message saying
  what changed and why.

If a rule seems to contradict the existing code, the rule wins — the code may be debt. Say so in
the notes instead of copying the deviation.

This document outlines the workflow, AI interactions, and manual interventions during the implementation of the Currency Details screen, strictly following the required reporting contract.



1. \###Actually Used Tools and Models

- \*\*

AI Models & Agents\*\*: Used an AI coding assistant (Codex/LLM) for iterative code generation and refactoring.

- \*\*

Development Tools\*\*: Android Studio / IntelliJ IDEA for codebase navigation and inspection.

- \*\*

Diagnostics\*\*: CLI tools (\`curl\`) and \`adb logcat\` for manual network probing and API contract verification.

- \*\*

Core Frameworks\*\*: KMP, MVIKotlin, Decompose, kotlin-inject, Kotest.



\### 2. How the Project Context Was Provided

- \*\*

Iterative Prompting\*\*: Context was not dumped at once. It was provided through sequential, stage-by-stage prompts (Domain $\to$ MVI $\to$ UI).

- \*\*

Strict Boundary Constraints\*\*: The AI was explicitly instructed to follow existing project patterns (e.g., "use existing \`RatesList\` patterns", "use \`BigDecimal\` with \`HALF_UP\`", "strictly stick to \`:shared:testAndroidHostTest\`").

- \*\*

Documentation Feeds\*\*: The contents of \`docs/screen.md\` and existing file structures were summarized into the prompts to establish the architectural boundaries.



\### 3. Real Agent Errors and Detection Methods

- \*\*

Error 1: Unauthorized Contract Migration\*\*: To "fix" origin server timeouts (521/522), the AI unilaterally attempted to change the API signatures and migrate the app to Frankfurter API v2.

-   \*

Detection\*: Manual code review of the \`git diff\` revealed modified DTOs and endpoints, violating the strict "Frankfurter API v1" requirement.

- \*\*

Error 2: Incorrect Query Parameter\*\*: The AI used the \`base\` parameter for time-series queries instead of the v1-required \`from\` parameter.

-   \*

Detection\*: Manual terminal testing (\`curl -i\`) and analyzing Ktor stream failures (\`[body is not available]\`) via \`adb logcat\`.

- \*\*

Error 3: Scope Creep (UI Tests)\*\*: The AI attempted to introduce automated Compose UI tests.

-   \*

Detection\*: Reviewing the generated test scopes, which violated the instruction to use only the existing unit test setup.



\### 4. Actually Performed Manual Fixes

- \*\*

Reverted AI Migrations\*\*: Manually rolled back the AI's unauthorized switch to API v2, restoring the v1 contract.

- \*\*

Engineered the Fallback Strategy\*\*: Manually designed and dictated the logic to intercept 5xx/timeouts and fallback to \`/v1/latest\` (adapting \`previousRate\` to nullable) to prevent app crashes.

- \*\*

API Parameter Correction\*\*: Formulated the prompt to specifically enforce the \`from\` parameter for the timeseries endpoint based on manual \`curl\` findings.

- \*\*

Code Review Refactoring (P3)\*\*: Manually extracted magic strings across test classes into \`companion object\` constants to improve maintainability after the AI generated inline strings.

# Commands

All modules except `:androidApp` are Kotlin Multiplatform, so the Android task names differ
from a plain Android project: there is no `testDebugUnitTest` in `:shared`.

| What                         | Command                                         |
|------------------------------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Compile the shared code      | `./gradlew :shared:compileAndroidMain`          |
| Unit tests                   | `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest`         |
| Static analysis              | `./gradlew detekt`                              |
| Build the APK                | `./gradlew :androidApp:assembleDebug`           |
| Install on a device/emulator | `./gradlew :androidApp:installDebug`            |

Test reports: `shared/build/reports/tests/testAndroidHostTest/index.html`.
Detekt report: `shared/build/reports/detekt/detekt.html`.

## Before calling a change done

1. `./gradlew :shared:testAndroidHostTest detekt :androidApp:assembleDebug` is green.
2. The app was launched and the changed screen was looked at, including the loading and error
   states (airplane mode is enough for the error).
# Architecture

## Modules

| Module       | What it is                                                                  |
|--------------|-----------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `:shared`    | Kotlin Multiplatform library (Android + iOS targets). All the app's code.  |
| `:androidApp`| The Android application: `MainActivity` builds the root component and shows it. |

The iOS targets exist so that `commonMain` cannot use `java.*` or `android.*`. Building an iOS
app is not needed.

## Packages of `:shared`

```text
com.fxrates
├── core/        ← helpers with no knowledge of features
│   ├── format/  ← NumberFormatter: the only place numbers become strings
│   ├── money/   ← arithmetic on rates (RateChangeCalculator)
│   └── utils/   ← Resource, resourceFlow, String.Empty
├── domain/      ← pure models and repository interfaces; no Ktor, no Compose, no DTOs
│   ├── model/
│   └── repository/
├── data/        ← everything that talks to the outside world
│   ├── remote/  ← FrankfurterApi (Ktor), DTOs, the HTTP client
│   └── repository/ ← repository implementations and DTO → domain converters
├── feature/<feature>/<screen>/ ← screens, see screen.md
├── root/        ← the navigation stack of the app
├── ui/          ← AppTheme, Strings
└── di/          ← AppComponent: the kotlin-inject graph
```

Dependencies point one way: `feature → domain ← data`. A screen sees `domain` interfaces and
models only — never a DTO, never `FrankfurterApi`, never `HttpClient`.

## Data

- The API is [Frankfurter](https://frankfurter.dev) (`https://api.frankfurter.dev/v1/`), ECB
  reference rates, no key. Rates exist for business days only: weekends and holidays have no
  entry, so "the last 30 days" is fewer than 30 points.
- An endpoint is a method of `FrankfurterApi` returning a DTO from `data/remote/dto`.
- A DTO is converted into a domain model in `data/repository/*Converter`, never in the screen.
- Numbers from the API become `BigDecimal` (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`) in the converter,
  through the string form, so the decimal digits the API sent are kept.
- A repository is an interface in `domain/repository` and an `*Impl` in `data/repository`, bound
  in `AppComponent`. A new read for an existing data source is a new method on the existing
  repository, not a new repository.

## Dependency injection

kotlin-inject. A class with an `@Inject` constructor needs no registration. An interface is
bound in `di/AppComponent.kt` with a `@Provides fun Impl.bindX(): X = this`. Long-lived objects
(the HTTP client, repositories) are `@AppScope`.

A Decompose component is created through an `@AssistedFactory`: the `ComponentContext`, the
screen arguments and the `Callbacks` are `@Assisted`, everything else is injected.
# Anatomy of a screen

Reference implementation: `feature/rates/list/`.

## Files

```text
feature/<feature>/<screen>/
├── mvi/
│   ├── XxxStore.kt          ← Intent / Action / Message / Label / State
│   ├── XxxReducer.kt        ← pure State.reduce(Message)
│   ├── XxxExecutor.kt       ← side effects
│   └── XxxStoreFactory.kt   ← assembles the Store, starts loading via a Bootstrapper
├── model/                   ← @Immutable UI models (rows, sections)
├── XxxUiState.kt            ← @Immutable state the composables draw
├── XxxUiStateConverter.kt   ← Store.State → UiState
├── XxxUiComponent.kt        ← abstract contract + Default (Factory, Callbacks)
├── XxxUiContent.kt          ← composables
└── XxxUiStatePreviewProvider.kt ← preview states
```

## Data flow

```text
Compose ─click─► UiComponent ─accept(Intent)─► Executor ─forward(Action)─► Executor ─► Repository
                                                   │                          │
                                              publish(Label)           dispatch(Message)
                                                   ▼                          ▼
                                     UiComponent → Callbacks        Reducer → State
                                                                              ▼
                                                     UiStateConverter → UiState → Compose
```

## MVI rules

- `Intent`, `Action`, `Message`, `Label` are nested `sealed class`es of the Store.
- **`State` holds domain models**, wrapped in `Resource` when they are loaded. No strings for
  display, no Compose types.
- **The Reducer is pure**: an expression-body `when` over every `Message`, only `copy(...)`.
- **`executeIntent` only does `dispatch`, `publish` and `forward`.** It may read `state()`.
- **Every side effect starts in `executeAction`**, and `executeAction` never reads `state()`: the
  Action carries everything it needs.
- A repository call is always `resourceFlow { repository.x() }.onEach { dispatch(...) }.launchIn(scope)`
  — never a bare `scope.launch { }` and never `runCatching`.
- A handler is named after its Intent/Action: `Action.LoadRates` → `loadRates(action)`. No
  `handle…`, `process…`, `do…`.
- Initial loading goes through `SimpleBootstrapper(Action.Load…)` in the factory.

## UiState and the converter

- `UiState` contains only what the screen draws, already formatted: strings, flags, UI models.
- All formatting and derived values are computed in `XxxUiStateConverter` through
  `NumberFormatter` and `core/money`. A composable never formats or calculates.
- A loading / error / content alternative is a sealed `Content` inside the `UiState`.

## UiComponent

- `abstract class XxxUiComponent` exposes `state: StateFlow<XxxUiState>` and one function per
  user action. The composable only knows this contract.
- `XxxUiComponentDefault` owns the Store, maps `states` through the converter and turns `Label`s
  into `Callbacks` calls.

## Navigation

- The stack lives in `root/RootUiComponent.kt`: a `@Serializable sealed class Config` and a
  `Child` per screen.
- **A screen does not navigate.** It publishes a `Label`, its component calls a `Callbacks`
  method, and the root pushes a `Config`.
- **A `Config` carries identifiers, not models** (`code`, `base`), so it survives process death.
  The destination screen loads what it needs itself.
- Back is handled by the stack (`handleBackButton = true`); a screen's own back button calls a
  `Callbacks` method, and the root pops.

## Tests

Every screen has at least:

- a **Store test** — a real Store from `XxxStoreFactory` with `DefaultStoreFactory()` and a fake
  repository; asserts `store.state` and the published labels after intents;
- a **UiStateConverter test** — State in, UiState out; this is where the formatted strings and
  the edge cases (empty data, nulls, zero) are checked.

See `RatesListStoreTest` and `RatesListUiStateConverterTest`.
# Code conventions

## Kotlin

- **No `it` in lambdas.** Name the parameter (`{ rate -> rate.code }`) or use a reference
  (`map(CurrencyRate::code)`). Names are full words: `rate`, not `r`.
- **Lambda properties and `invoke` operators are called explicitly:** `onClick.invoke()`.
- **`String.Empty`** (`core/utils`) instead of `""` in State, UiState and converters.
- **`sealed class`**, not `sealed interface`, for closed hierarchies.
- **Braces in a `when` are uniform:** if one branch is a block, all are.
- **Expression body** only when the body fits on one line; a trailing lambda
  (`= Column { … }`, `= when (x) { … }`) is fine.
- Constants: a top-level `const val` is `UpperCamelCase`; inside an `object` or a
  `companion object` it is `SCREAMING_SNAKE_CASE`.
- Lines are at most 120 characters. An empty line after the opening `{` and before the closing
  `}` of a class body.
- KDoc only where it says something the signature does not: a unit, why a value is nullable, an
  invariant. Comments are in English.

## Money and numbers

- **Rates and everything derived from them are `BigDecimal`** (`com.ionspin.kotlin.bignum`).
  `Double` and `Float` are not used for rates, amounts or their changes: binary floating point
  cannot represent most decimal fractions.
- Numbers become strings only through `core/format/NumberFormatter`. No `toString()` of a
  number in UI code, no hand-made rounding.
- A percent is shown with two decimals and an explicit sign (`+1.23%`, `-0.50%`); a value that
  rounds to zero has no sign (`0.00%`).

## Compose

- Spacing comes from `AppTheme.spacing`, semantic colours (up / down / neutral) from
  `AppTheme.colors`, text styles from `MaterialTheme.typography`. No literal `dp` and no literal
  `Color` in a screen.
- User-facing strings are in `ui/Strings.kt`, never inline in a composable.
- The public composable takes the component; it collects the state and delegates to a private
  stateless overload that takes `UiState` and lambdas. Previews render the stateless overload
  with states from the `PreviewParameterProvider`.
- Callbacks are named after the event: `onCurrencyClick`, `onRefresh`, `onBack`.

## Tests

- kotest, `FunSpec`, in `shared/src/commonTest`. Matchers from `io.kotest.matchers`.
- Fakes, not mocks: a hand-written `Fake…Repository` in `commonTest/.../testing`.
- Code that runs on `Dispatchers.Main` gets `Dispatchers.setMain(...)` in `beforeSpec` and
  `resetMain()` in `afterSpec`.
- A test name says the behaviour, not the method: `"a failed load ends in an error"`.

# AGENTS.md

Rules for anyone — human or AI agent — changing this repository. They are not suggestions: a
change that ignores them is reviewed as wrong even if it works.

## Read before writing code

| Document                                       | Open it when                                                  |
|------------------------------------------------|---------------------------------------------------------------|
| [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) | Deciding where code goes; adding a model, an endpoint, a repository method |
| [`docs/screen.md`](docs/screen.md)             | Touching any layer of a screen: Store, Executor, UiState, UiComponent, navigation |
| [`docs/conventions.md`](docs/conventions.md)   | Writing any Kotlin or Compose code                            |
| [`docs/commands.md`](docs/commands.md)         | Building, testing, checking the result                        |

`RatesList` (`shared/src/commonMain/kotlin/com/fxrates/feature/rates/list/`) is the reference
screen. A new screen has the same files, the same naming and the same layering.

## Ground rules

- **The stack is fixed:** Kotlin Multiplatform, Compose Multiplatform, Decompose, MVIKotlin,
  kotlin-inject, Ktor, kotlinx.serialization, kotest. No Hilt/Koin, no AndroidX ViewModel, no
  Retrofit, no mocking library. A new dependency needs a reason, and the reason is written in the

change that ignores them is reviewed as wrong even if it works.

## Read before writing code

screen. A new screen has the same files, the same naming and the same layering.

  Retrofit, no mocking library. A new dependency needs a reason, and the reason is written in the
  PR / solution notes.

This document outlines the workflow, AI interactions, and manual interventions during the implementation of the Currency Details screen, strictly following the required reporting contract.

### 1. Actually Used Tools and Models

- **AI Models & Agents**: Used an AI coding assistant (Codex/LLM) for iterative code generation and refactoring.
- **Development Tools**: Android Studio / IntelliJ IDEA for codebase navigation and inspection.
- **Diagnostics**: CLI tools (`curl`) and `adb logcat` for manual network probing and API contract verification.
- **Core Frameworks**: KMP, MVIKotlin, Decompose, kotlin-inject, Kotest.

- **Reverted AI Migrations**: Manually rolled back the AI's unauthorized switch to API v2, restoring the v1 contract.

- **Code Review Refactoring (P3)**: Manually extracted magic strings across test classes into `companion object` constants to improve maintainability after the AI generated inline strings.
